blocks.tamil_translation: everything, and I know nothing; You are the One who knows the unseen well. O Allah! If You know this matter to be good for my Deen, for my worldly life and for the end of my life, then grant it to me and make it easy for me! Then put barakah in it too! If You know this matter not to be good for my Deen, for my worldly life and for the end of my life, then turn this matter away from me and turn me away from this matter! Whatever matter is good for me, wherever it may be, grant it to me! Then make me content and at peace with that matter!" — the narrator says that the Prophet ﷺ said that in the du'a one should name the matter one intends, saying it is such-and-such a matter.

blocks.text: Note:- If one is to make Istikharah for a journey, one should say "hadhas-safar", or if one is to make Istikharah for a marriage, one should say "hadhan-nikah". If one does not know how to say it in Arabic, then at both places in the du'a where "hadhal-amr" occurs, one should bring to mind the matter for which one is making Istikharah.

blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرَةَ ﵁ قَالَ: خَسَفَتِ الشَّمْسُ عَلَي عَهْدِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ فَخَرَجَ يَجُرُّ رِدَاءَهُ حَتَّي انْتَهَي إِلَي الْمَسْجِدِ وَثَابَ النَّاسُ إِلَيْهِ فَصَلَّي بِهِمْ رَكْعَتَيْنِ، فَانْجَلَتِ الشَّمْسُ فَقَالَ: إِنَّ الشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ آيَتَانِ مِنْ آيَاتِ اللهِ وَإِنَّهُمَا لَا يَخْسِفَانِ لِمَوْتِ أَحَدٍ، وَإِذَا كَانَ ذلِكَ فَصَلُّوا وَادْعُوا حَتَّي يَنْكَشِفَ مَا بِكُمْ، وَذلِكَ أَنَّ ابْناً للِنَّبِيِّ ﷺ مَاتَ يُقَالُ لَهُ: إِبْرَاهِيمُ فَقَالَ النَّاسُ فِي ذلِكَ.
